specAnchors.text: understand how division of a cell by meiosis produces four cells, each with half the number of chromosomes, and that this results in the formation of genetically different haploid gametes

primer.text: Sex cells need half a chromosome set each, and building them takes two divisions. This note walks meiosis from chromosome doubling through both splits to four genetically different haploid daughters, then sets the comparison table beside mitosis so you can quote the differences the examiner asks for.

modules.title: Two Divisions, Four Different Daughters
modules.opening: Meiosis is the division that builds gametes: the chromosomes double first, two rounds of division follow, and four daughter cells emerge, each carrying half the starting number and each genetically distinct from its siblings.
keyPoints: Meiosis is a nuclear division producing cells that are genetically different.
Chromosomes double before the divisions, as they do before mitosis.
The first division separates chromosome pairs; the second separates the copies.
Four haploid daughter cells result, each with one chromosome of each pair.
Halving matters because fertilisation would otherwise double the chromosome count.

low.restatement: The cell divides twice and ends up with four cells, each holding half the chromosomes.
low.analogy: A library lending half its collection to four branches, no two branches identical.
low.examPointer: The count is four, the content is half, and the products differ.

medium.restatement: Pairing then separation in two rounds guarantees the halving and reshuffles the genetic material.
medium.analogy: Two sorting rounds at a mail depot: first the pairs are split, then the copies.
medium.examPointer: Attach a reason to the halving: fertilisation restores the full set.

modules.title: Mitosis and Meiosis Side by Side
modules.opening: The comparison table sets the two divisions side by side, and exams love the differences, so anchor on the ones the table stresses: daughter cell number, chromosome content, genetic identity of products, and the jobs each division does.
keyPoints: Mitosis yields two identical diploid cells; meiosis yields four different haploid cells.
Mitosis drives growth and repair; meiosis builds gametes for reproduction.
Only meiosis runs two divisions; mitosis runs one.
Examiners reward specific differences, so quote numbers and outcomes.

low.restatement: One division clones for maintenance; two divisions halve for reproduction.
low.analogy: A photocopier versus a card dealer: one duplicates exactly, the other deals varied hands.
low.examPointer: Give two or three differences and be specific, as the table demands.

medium.restatement: Number, ploidy and identity move together: two divisions are what allow the halving and the variation.
medium.analogy: Two taps drain a tank lower than one; the extra division is what halves the set.
medium.examPointer: Know the reason behind each difference, not just the difference.

glossary.definition: The two-stage division that produces four genetically different haploid cells.
A haploid sex cell produced by meiosis, such as sperm or egg.
Carrying half the normal chromosome number.
Carrying the full double chromosome set.
The single division that produces identical diploid cells.
